question: What is the primary purpose of barrier nursing?

options.A: To completely cure chronic infectious diseases
options.B: To stop pathogens from spreading between people
options.C: To speed up the healing of surgical wounds
options.D: To replace the need for routine handwashing

explanation: Barrier nursing uses physical blocks to prevent germs from moving from one person or surface to another. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h1)

question: Why are hospital-acquired infections a major concern for nurses using barriers?

options.B: Hospital germs are easily spread to vulnerable patients
options.C: Patients bring all their own germs from home

explanation: Sick patients in hospitals have lowered immune defenses, making them very easy targets for spreading germs if barriers are missed. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h1)

question: The place where a microorganism normally lives and multiplies is called what?
explanation: A reservoir provides a safe home for pathogens to survive and multiply before finding a new host. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h2)

question: How does washing your hands thoroughly break the chain of infection?

options.A: It removes the susceptible host entirely
options.C: It stops the mode of transmission
options.D: It destroys the infectious agent completely

explanation: Hand hygiene removes germs from your hands, preventing them from traveling from one patient or surface to another. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h2)

question: Which type of isolation is used to protect a patient with a very weak immune system?
explanation: Protective or reverse isolation guards patients who cannot fight off everyday germs by keeping outside microorganisms away from them. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h3)

question: A patient with a wound infected by a multi-drug resistant organism needs which type of precaution?
explanation: Resistant germs in open wounds are typically passed through physical touch, making contact isolation necessary. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h3)

question: Who should be cared for using standard precautions in a hospital?

options.A: Every patient, regardless of their diagnosis
options.B: Patients admitted to surgical wards only
options.C: Only patients with confirmed viral infections
options.D: Only individuals coughing or showing rashes

explanation: Standard precautions are universal and must be applied to all patients because infection status is not always known upfront. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h4)

question: When are transmission-based precautions added to patient care?

options.A: Only after laboratory tests prove the patient is cured
options.B: When the hospital runs out of standard gloves
options.C: When a specific contagious disease is suspected or confirmed
options.D: Whenever a visitor enters the isolation room

explanation: Transmission-based precautions are extra steps added on top of standard rules when dealing with specific, easily spread germs. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h4)

question: When putting on a full set of PPE, which item is typically put on first?
explanation: The gown is put on first to cover your clothing, followed by masks, eye protection, and gloves last. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h5)

question: Why must you perform hand hygiene immediately after taking off your gloves?

options.A: Hospital policy requires washing hands twice per hour
options.B: Gloves make your hands smell unpleasant
options.C: Microorganisms may have transferred to your skin during removal
options.D: It helps the skin dry out after sweating inside rubber

explanation: Even with careful removal, tiny tears or contact with the outside of gloves can transfer germs to your hands. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h5)

question: Where should used injection needles and sharp blades be discarded?
explanation: Sharps must go directly into rigid, puncture-resistant containers to prevent accidental needle pricks. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h6)

question: What is the main reason for frequently cleaning high-touch surfaces in an isolation room?

options.A: To prevent germs from surviving on objects and spreading
options.B: To prevent medical equipment from rusting
options.C: To make the floor shiny and slip-resistant
options.D: To keep the room smelling fresh for visitors

explanation: Pathogens can live on dry surfaces for hours or days, making regular disinfection vital to stopping indirect spread. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h6)

question: How do patients in isolation often feel due to lack of human contact?
explanation: Being cut off from normal social interaction and seeing staff in heavy gear frequently causes emotional distress. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h7)

question: A patient in strict isolation cries because no one wants to touch them without gear. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Assure them that the infection is not serious at all
options.B: Remove your gown and gloves to prove you care
options.C: Tell them the rules are necessary and leave the room quickly
options.D: Acknowledge their feelings and spend time talking calmly with them

explanation: Validating emotions and offering supportive conversation helps reduce the psychological toll of isolation while keeping safety intact. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h7)

question: What is a key daily responsibility of the nurse regarding barrier nursing?

options.D: Ensuring proper compliance with infection control rules

explanation: Nurses must actively monitor and maintain infection control standards during every shift to protect patients and staff. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h8)

question: What should a nurse do if a visitor enters an isolation room without wearing the required PPE?

options.A: Ignore it if they promise not to touch the patient
options.B: Ask another staff member to handle the situation later
options.C: Report the visitor to hospital security immediately
options.D: Politely stop them, explain the rules, and help them put on PPE

explanation: Educating visitors and ensuring they wear correct gear prevents breaches in the barrier system. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h8)
